translation_en:
Al-Tabari says that God addresses His prophet Muhammad. According to what has been related, the polytheists among his people offered to worship God for one year on condition that God's prophet worship their gods for one year. God therefore revealed the reply: 'Say,' Muhammad, to these polytheists who asked you to worship their gods for one year in return for their worshipping your God for one year: 'O disbelievers' in God, 'I do not worship what you worship' of gods and idols now; 'nor do you worship what I worship' now; 'nor will I be a worshipper,' in the future, 'of what you have worshipped' in the past; 'nor will you ever worship,' in your future, 'what I worship' now and in the future.

This wording was used because God's address to His messenger concerned particular individuals among the polytheists whom He knew would never believe. This had already been established in His prior knowledge. He instructed His prophet to make them abandon their hope and expectation of the proposed arrangement: it would never happen on either side at any time. He also removed the prophet's hope that they would believe or ever prosper. They remained so: some were killed by the sword at Badr, and others died before that as disbelievers.

The interpreters expressed an explanation similar to ours, and transmitted reports convey it.

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi related to me: Abu Khalaf related to us: Dawud related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: Quraysh promised God's messenger money that would make him the richest man in Mecca, marriage to whichever women he wanted, and that they would follow him. They said: 'This is what we offer you, Muhammad. Stop insulting our gods and speaking ill of them. If you will not, we propose one arrangement beneficial to both you and us.' He asked: 'What is it?' They said: 'Worship our gods, al-Lat and al-Uzza, for one year, and we will worship your God for one year.' He said: 'Until I see what comes from my Lord.' Revelation then came from the Preserved Tablet: 'Say, O disbelievers,' the surah. God also revealed: 'Say: Is it other than God that you command me to worship, O ignorant ones?' through 'Worship, then, and be among the grateful.'

Yaqub related to me: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Said ibn Mina, the client of al-Bakhtari, related to me: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-As ibn Wail, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf met God's messenger and said: 'Muhammad, come: let us worship what you worship, and you worship what we worship. We will include you in our whole undertaking. If what you have brought is better than what we possess, we will have shared in it with you and received our portion of it. If what we possess is better than what you possess, you will have shared in our undertaking and received your portion of it.' God then revealed 'Say, O disbelievers' through the end of the surah.
